extra.message: Sensitive data exposure: when a query returns more than one row, run_sql_query() returns {'users': _data} where _data holds raw tuples from 'SELECT *' queries that include the password column (index 3). Unlike the single-row branch (lines 155-160), which deliberately omits the password field, multi-row responses leak MD5 password hashes to unauthenticated callers of GET /select (e.g., when a username matches two users or via the documented '" OR 1=1' payload).

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: SQL injection: the user-supplied 'username' query parameter of the GET /select endpoint is interpolated directly into the f-string f'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";' (line 182), which is executed by db.execute(query) in run_sql_query() (line 146) without parameterization. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. /select?username=" OR 1=1; -- to dump the entire users table.

Weak password hashing: user passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (md5(user.password.encode()).hexdigest() at line 187; the same weak scheme is used for seeded data at line 113). MD5 is fast and cryptographically broken, so stored password hashes are trivially brute-forced or looked up in rainbow tables; a slow salted hash (bcrypt/scrypt/argon2) is required.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: SQL injection: all user-controlled fields of the User model (name, username, password, address, email, contact) from the PUT /user request body are interpolated unescaped into an INSERT statement built with an f-string (lines 188-204) and executed via db.execute(query) (line 146). Pydantic only enforces str types, so any field containing a double quote (e.g. name='x", "dummy") allows injection of arbitrary SQL into the INSERT.

NoSQL injection: the POST /find endpoint takes the raw JSON request body (query = await request.json(), line 224) and passes it directly as the MontyDB/MongoDB query filter to users.find(query) via get_nosql_users() (line 171). An attacker can inject query operators such as {"username": {"$ne": ""}} or {"id": {"$in": [1,2]}} to bypass the intended equality filter and enumerate arbitrary records from the collection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Used in a Database Query ('NoSQL Injection')

extra.message: Missing authorization / broken access control: the DELETE /user endpoint allows any unauthenticated client to delete arbitrary users by supplying a 'username' query parameter (lines 229-232) or a User body with an 'address' (lines 233-235). There is no authentication, ownership, or permission check, so anonymous attackers can destroy other users' records at will.

SQL injection: the user-supplied 'username' query parameter of the DELETE /user endpoint is interpolated directly into f'DELETE FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";' (line 231) and executed via db.execute(query) (line 146). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL predicates (e.g. username=" OR 1=1; --) to delete or affect arbitrary rows.

SQL injection: the user-supplied 'address' field from the request body is interpolated into f'DELETE FROM users WHERE address = {user.address};' (line 235) without even surrounding quotes. The attacker fully controls the SQL tokens and can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. address='1 OR 1=1; --') to delete arbitrary rows.

Missing authentication for critical function: the POST /reset endpoint deletes both database files (remove() and rmtree() at lines 244-245) and reinitializes them, with no authentication or authorization check of any kind. Any unauthenticated client can wipe all application data, causing complete denial of service.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
